classification_rationale: the documented recovery path cannot complete

trigger: the DSN password-extraction sed added by this change: disaster-recovery.md cron job #2 and restore step 3, on any DSN that is percent-encoded, passwordless, keyword-conninfo, or contains an @
summary: The new snippets extract the password with sed -E 's!^[a-z]+://[^:/@]*:([^@]*)@.*$!\1!' and silently produce wrong credentials. All four cases EMPIRICALLY RUN by the reporter: percent-encoded 'p%40ss' -> PGPASSWORD=[p%40ss] (libpq decodes URIs but PGPASSWORD is literal, so auth fails); passwordless DSN -> PGPASSWORD=[postgresql://yuzu@db:5432/yuzu] (the whole URI sent as a password where none was needed); keyword conninfo 'host=... password=...' -> no match, whole string as password; password containing '@' -> truncated to 'a' and DSN_NOPASS corrupted to 'postgresql://yuzu@b@db:5432/yuzu'. In cron the failure goes to unread root mail while jobs #1 and #3 still succeed, so a dated backup directory EXISTS containing 2 of 3 artefacts - the operator has a backup that looks complete and has no database dump. Chaos: point the cron at a %-encoded DSN; assert the dated dir contains yuzu-pg.dump.
classification_rationale: shipped operator snippet produces a wrong result on ordinary inputs
